extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, new inventors, small businesses, and entrepreneurs unfamiliar with patents
extracted.subtask_description: Overview guidance describing what patents are and the essential steps to apply for, obtain, manage, and enforce patent rights in the U.S. Intended for people who know little or nothing about patents and need an end-to-end introduction and pointers to resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent essentials
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level information explaining 'What is a patent?' and providing assistance with the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introductory orientation to patents for people who know nothing about them; establishes foundational concepts before diving into application and post-grant topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic questions about patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers to common foundational questions about patents (what they are, what they protect, who can apply, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to determine basic eligibility, rights conferred, and common terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign patents and treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about international patent rights, how foreign patents and treaties interact with U.S. patenting, and cross-border filing considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for applicants considering protection outside the U.S. and for understanding treaty-related deadlines and options (e.g., PCT/Paris Convention implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources and help available to inventors, including where to get help understanding the patent process and preparing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to USPTO assistance programs and other support tailored for inventors unfamiliar with patent procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of the agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of USPTO roles and responsibilities in examining, granting, and administering patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies what the agency can and cannot do for applicants and patent owners (e.g., examination, record-keeping, not legal advice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the application process, including submission, required elements, and steps taken by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights key application-phase considerations such as formality requirements and procedural steps applicants must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations about legal representation when filing for a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when and why to use a registered patent attorney or agent and how representation affects filing and prosecution; points to 'Attorneys and agents' resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on critical deadlines (filing windows, maintenance/payment windows, PCT/priority deadlines) and the fees associated with patent prosecution and maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the importance of meeting deadlines and paying required fees to preserve rights; use USPTO fee schedules and calendar tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions and encouragement to search existing patents and published applications to identify prior art and refine claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use USPTO search tools (and other databases) to conduct prior-art searches before filing; searching helps assess novelty and avoid unnecessary filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorneys and agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about the roles of registered patent attorneys and agents and how to locate and engage them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on choosing qualified representatives, their responsibilities, and how they assist with drafting and prosecuting applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of different patent types (e.g., utility, design, plant) and which subject matter each protects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps applicants determine which patent type fits their invention and informs drafting and claim strategy appropriate to that type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of application paths (e.g., provisional, nonprovisional, PCT international filings, continuations) and their uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains strategic choices among application types, priority claims, and timing implications for protection and prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination process
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of how patent applications are examined by the USPTO, including office actions, responses, and allowance or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes typical prosecution workflow, how examiners apply legal standards, and what applicants can expect during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ready to file
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on preparatory steps and checks applicants should complete before filing an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers preparedness items such as necessary disclosures, claim drafting, drawings, inventor declarations, and fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing your patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant guidance on how to maintain, enforce, transfer, and protect patent rights after grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers lifecycle activities from grant through enforcement and transfer, including administrative actions owners should take to preserve and use rights effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of the legal nature and scope of the rights conferred by a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that a patent grants exclusionary rights (not affirmative rights to practice) and discusses territorial and temporal limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about marking a product with patent numbers and the legal and practical effects of marking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains benefits of marking (e.g., notice to the public) and correct practices for marking products and packaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on circumstances and procedures to obtain extensions of patent term (e.g., regulatory delays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes eligibility, available mechanisms (such as patent term adjustment or extension), and timing for filing requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and schedules for paying maintenance (renewal) fees to keep a patent in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that failure to pay maintenance fees results in lapse of rights and points to schedules, grace periods, and recovery options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for correcting errors in patents or patent applications (e.g., certificate of correction, reissue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on when to use different correction mechanisms and the substantive limits on corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and considerations for patent ownership, inventorship, and title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how ownership is established, inventor obligations, assignment recording, and how ownership affects enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments and licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on transferring patent rights by assignment and licensing arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers required documentation and recording of assignments/licenses and practical considerations for negotiating and documenting transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of what constitutes patent infringement and basic enforcement options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how infringement is determined, remedies available, and when to seek legal counsel for enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpful resources for new customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Pointers to USPTO resources, events, videos, and tools designed to help new applicants navigate the patent process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes training events (e.g., Path to a Patent sessions), videos on innovation cycles, and online tools to identify IP types and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access free patent services
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of free services the USPTO and partners provide to help applicants (e.g., pro bono programs, search assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages eligible applicants to use free resources to reduce cost and improve application quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review online patent tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to review and use online USPTO tools for searching, filing, and managing patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points users to specific online utilities for examination status checks, filing portals, and fee payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview of the patent process
rubrics_metrics.description: A step-by-step conceptual overview from identifying an invention through filing, examination, grant, and post-grant management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a roadmap for first-time applicants to understand sequence and dependencies of actions required to obtain and maintain a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify if you have a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools and guidance to determine whether an invention qualifies for patent protection and whether an issued patent already exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use decision tools and searches to assess patentability (novelty, usefulness, subject-matter eligibility) and to locate existing patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigating the IP process / Find resources for small businesses and entrepreneurs
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeted guidance and links for small businesses and entrepreneurs to navigate intellectual property processes and access support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes business-focused resources, programs, and workshops to help early-stage companies make IP decisions and manage filings.
